Title: Condominium declaration review
Summary: Build a cited issue matrix from a declaration and amendments.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium counsel conducting due diligence for [buyer or lender]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [attach declaration], [amendments], [property/transaction context], [review date].
TASK: Identify provisions on unit boundaries, common elements, limited common elements, maintenance, insurance, leasing, voting, amendment, and termination. Reconcile conflicting amendments.
OUTPUT: An issue matrix with document/page, operative language, practical effect, question for counsel, and priority. Quote only short necessary excerpts. Identify missing exhibits and any provision requiring a current Chapter 718 check.

Title: Condominium board vote analysis
Summary: Map quorum, voting and notice questions to governing sources.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium association counsel advising the board
PromptBody:
CONTEXT: [meeting facts], [governing documents], [dates], [minutes and notices].
TASK: Analyze whether the proposed Florida condominium board action followed applicable notice, quorum, and voting requirements. Start with a dated chronology; distinguish what the documents say from current statutory requirements.
OUTPUT: Issue / governing source / record fact / analysis / missing evidence / practical correction. Identify any issue that requires counsel to inspect the actual meeting record.

Title: Condominium records request triage
Summary: Organize a records demand and the response steps.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium association counsel preparing an official-records response
PromptBody:
INPUT: [owner request], [receipt date and method], [association record inventory], [prior response].
TASK: Sort each item requested into available, needs search, potentially restricted, and unclear. Check the applicable Florida condominium official-records rules as of [date]; do not assume every requested item is disclosable.
OUTPUT: A response decision tree, deadline calendar with stated assumptions, document collection checklist, and a concise draft acknowledgement for counsel review.

Title: Structural reserve decision memo
Summary: Frame board decisions from inspection and reserve records.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium association counsel preparing a board decision memo
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [building age and location], [inspection reports], [reserve study], [budget], [meeting materials].
TASK: Prepare a Florida condominium board memo on the documented repair and reserve decisions. Verify which current milestone-inspection and structural-integrity-reserve requirements apply before stating deadlines or funding duties.
OUTPUT: Executive decision list, evidence table, obligations to confirm, funding options stated as scenarios, and questions for the engineer and manager. Do not make engineering conclusions.

Title: Association insurance allocation
Summary: Compare declaration, policy, and statutory responsibility.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium counsel evaluating a documented casualty allocation
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [declaration], [insurance policy excerpts], [damage facts], [loss date].
TASK: Compare the allocation of insurance, repair, deductible, and owner responsibilities under the supplied documents and applicable Florida condominium law. Avoid deciding coverage without the actual policy and claim facts.
OUTPUT: A three-column comparison of source language, affected property, and responsibility; then list conflicts, carrier questions, and proposed next steps.

Title: Condominium lease restriction review
Summary: Assess restrictions and approval mechanics in context.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium counsel for [association or unit owner]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [declaration/bylaws/rules], [amendments], [proposed lease], [relevant unit history].
TASK: Identify operative Florida condominium lease restrictions, approval procedures, transfer fees, duration limits, and amendment or grandfathering issues. Trace each restriction to its source and effective date.
OUTPUT: Clause-by-clause table, open factual questions, and a short proposed client explanation. Flag any enforceability question for current authority research.

Title: HOA covenant enforcement file
Summary: Build an evenhanded enforcement record review.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel evaluating covenant enforcement
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [recorded covenants], [rules], [alleged violation], [photos/letters], [comparable enforcement history].
TASK: Evaluate the documented basis for a Florida HOA covenant enforcement decision, including notice, cure, hearing, and consistency issues where applicable. Keep allegations separate from proven facts.
OUTPUT: Evidence matrix, timeline, process checklist, weaknesses in the file, and a neutral notice outline for attorney review.

Title: HOA election process checklist
Summary: Organize election steps against actual documents.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel preparing an election checklist
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [governing documents], [election date], [notices], [nomination and ballot procedures].
TASK: Build a Florida HOA election checklist tailored to the supplied documents and current applicable law. Distinguish statutory requirements from document-specific requirements; do not assume condominium election rules apply.
OUTPUT: Date-driven checklist with source for each step, owner, required proof, and unresolved questions.

Title: Board recall chronology
Summary: Test service, voting, and meeting events.
RolePerspective: Florida association counsel assessing a proposed director recall
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [association type], [petition or ballots], [service evidence], [owner roster], [board meeting notice/minutes].
TASK: Construct a neutral chronology of a Florida association director recall. Identify disputed signatures, voting entitlements, service, timing, and replacement issues without assuming recall validity.
OUTPUT: Dated chronology, issue matrix with controlling source to verify, missing evidence, and immediate procedural decisions for counsel.

Title: Purchase agreement risk scan
Summary: Identify negotiated risk and unfilled business terms.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate counsel for [buyer or seller]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [purchase agreement], [exhibits], [deal summary], [client priorities].
TASK: Review diligence, title, survey, financing, representations, casualty, default, closing deliverables, and survival. Preserve the agreement's defined terms.
OUTPUT: Ranked risk matrix with clause reference, present wording, business impact, proposed revision, and negotiation priority. List missing exhibits and dates separately.

Title: Closing obligation tracker
Summary: Turn transaction documents into an actionable closing list.
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [signed agreement], [amendments], [title commitment], [lender checklist], [target closing date].
TASK: Extract each condition, notice, deliverable, funding step, and deadline. Reconcile amendments and distinguish explicit dates from calculated dates.
OUTPUT: Tracker columns: obligation, responsible party, source/page, trigger, due date or formula, status, and open question. Do not silently calculate a disputed deadline.

Title: Estoppel certificate reconciliation
Summary: Compare estoppel answers to contract and records.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate closing counsel reconciling association documents
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [association estoppel], [purchase contract], [ledger], [governing documents], [closing date].
TASK: Reconcile amounts, pending assessments, violations, approval requirements, transfer fees, and estoppel validity as shown in the supplied records. Verify any Florida statutory effect before drawing a legal conclusion.
OUTPUT: Discrepancy table with quoted source location, closing consequence, party to contact, and proposed resolution.

Title: Commercial lease issue list
Summary: Review a Florida commercial lease from one party’s position.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial leasing counsel for [landlord or tenant]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [lease], [term sheet], [property details], [negotiation priorities].
TASK: Compare economics, use, repairs, CAM, insurance, assignment, default, remedies, casualty, condemnation, options, and surrender against the term sheet.
OUTPUT: Clause reference, issue, practical risk, suggested revision, priority, and business input needed. Do not treat residential tenancy statutes as automatically applicable.

Title: Residential lease compliance inventory
Summary: Spot missing facts and provisions for Florida housing.
RolePerspective: Florida residential leasing counsel for [landlord or tenant]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [residential lease and addenda], [property location], [building age], [deposit arrangement], [proposed commencement].
TASK: Review a Florida residential lease for issues requiring current state or applicable federal law checks, including disclosures, deposits, access, fees, termination, and remedies. Do not assert that a disclosure applies without the relevant property facts.
OUTPUT: Ranked checklist with lease citation, authority to verify, proposed fix, and missing fact.

Title: Land use entitlement roadmap
Summary: Map approvals for a proposed Florida project.
RolePerspective: Florida land-use counsel advising the project team
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [parcel and jurisdiction], [proposed use], [zoning map/code], [prior approvals], [development schedule].
TASK: Identify apparent land use approval paths and threshold questions, distinguishing adopted text from staff practice or assumptions. Check the relevant local government sources and current Florida law if research is available.
OUTPUT: Permit/approval decision tree, likely sequence, dependencies, public-hearing points, and questions for planning staff. Do not guarantee entitlement.

Title: Title commitment exceptions
Summary: Turn Schedule B into a buyer action list.
RolePerspective: Florida buyer-side title counsel preparing a curative list
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [current title commitment], [recorded exception instruments], [contract], [buyer intended use].
TASK: Pair each Schedule B requirement and exception with its underlying instrument. Identify monetary liens, access or use restrictions, survey-dependent matters, and items needing insurer confirmation.
OUTPUT: Item number, recorded source, practical effect, curative request, responsible party, and priority. Do not conclude an exception is harmless without the instrument.

Title: Survey and title reconciliation
Summary: Identify gaps between survey callouts and recorded rights.
RolePerspective: Florida title counsel coordinating questions with a licensed surveyor
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [survey], [legal description], [title commitment], [recorded easements].
TASK: Reconcile parcel description, access, visible improvements, encroachments, easement locations, and survey notes. Identify issues requiring surveyor clarification or title insurer underwriting.
OUTPUT: Map-reference or survey-note / recorded-document / possible effect / person to resolve table. Do not give a surveyor's boundary opinion.

Title: Legal description comparison
Summary: Find textual conflicts in property descriptions.
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [deed description], [contract exhibit], [survey description], [prior recorded instrument].
TASK: Extract the point of beginning, calls, bearings, distances, parcel identifiers, exceptions, and exhibit references from each description. Compare exact wording and flag missing pages or inconsistent calls.
OUTPUT: Side-by-side difference table and questions for title counsel or surveyor. Do not infer that descriptions convey the same land from approximate wording alone.

Title: Civil complaint issue map
Summary: Evaluate allegations and supporting documents.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigator assessing an initial pleading
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [Florida civil complaint], [key contract/record documents], [client chronology], [service date].
TASK: Map each count, requested relief, factual allegation, and attached exhibit. Identify facial gaps, inconsistencies, potential response issues, and facts to investigate under current Florida procedure.
OUTPUT: Claim / alleged elements / cited paragraph / record support / response question table. Flag deadlines as unverified until service and any orders are checked.

Title: Discovery response workplan
Summary: Assign answers, objections, and collection tasks.
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [discovery requests], [service details], [case management order], [custodian list], [known repositories].
TASK: Classify each request by topic, likely custodian, collection source, privilege concern, proposed objection question, and needed client input. Verify current Florida procedural deadlines and any case-specific order.
OUTPUT: Request-by-request workplan and missing-data questions. Do not invent documents or waive objections by assuming facts.

Title: Motion response authority plan
Summary: Find controlling sources before drafting an opposition.
RolePerspective: Florida litigation research attorney preparing an opposition outline
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [opposing motion], [record excerpts], [court], [hearing date], [client objective].
TASK: Extract the motion's propositions and identify which require authority, factual rebuttal, or both. Research current primary Florida authority if available, checking procedural rules, appellate district, treatment, and case posture.
OUTPUT: Proposition / supporting citation claimed / verified authority / record response / research gap matrix, followed by an opposition outline. Never fabricate a case or quote.

Title: Deposition preparation outline
Summary: Build topic blocks tied to evidence and exhibits.
RolePerspective: Florida litigation counsel preparing a witness examination
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [pleadings], [witness role], [chronology], [production], [key exhibits].
TASK: Identify admissions to seek, disputed events, exhibit foundations, and follow-up paths. Separate known testimony from questions to test.
OUTPUT: Ordered topic blocks with objective, exhibit reference, primary question, follow-up, and impeachment source. Include a list of factual gaps for attorney preparation.

Title: Mediation exposure brief
Summary: Summarize litigation positions and settlement levers.
RolePerspective: Florida trial counsel preparing confidential mediation advice
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [pleadings], [evidence summary], [damages model], [offers], [client objectives].
TASK: Present the strongest and weakest documented points for each side. Build best, central, and adverse scenarios with stated assumptions, without inventing probabilities or recoveries.
OUTPUT: One-page confidential preparation brief, scenario table, nonmonetary terms to consider, and decisions requiring client authority.

Title: Client intake questions
Summary: Turn a real estate problem into a focused fact interview.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate attorney preparing an intake interview
PromptBody:
CONTEXT: [short client description], [property type], [desired outcome], [known dates].
TASK: Generate a concise first-call question sequence for a Florida real estate matter. Ask threshold questions first, then documents, timeline, counterparties, financial exposure, and urgency.
OUTPUT: No more than 15 grouped questions, each marked essential or follow-up, plus a requested-document list. Avoid assuming the client has a viable claim.

Title: Client update email
Summary: Convert a verified matter record into a clear update.
RolePerspective: Client-service attorney drafting a plain-language matter update
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [verified status notes], [completed work], [open decisions], [dates], [client audience].
TASK: Draft a concise Florida matter update in plain language. Put the decision requested from the client near the top; distinguish completed work, next steps, and contingent dates.
OUTPUT: Subject line and email of about 200–300 words. Do not add assurances or legal conclusions absent from the verified notes; leave placeholders for missing information.

Title: Redline instruction set
Summary: Produce precise proposed clause edits for counsel.
RolePerspective: Florida transactional real-estate attorney revising a negotiated clause
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [existing provision], [document definitions], [negotiation goal], [nonnegotiable terms], [which party represented].
TASK: Identify ambiguity and unintended consequences, then provide a revised provision that fits the document's style and defined terms. Do not silently change unrelated economics.
OUTPUT: Issue list, clean replacement clause, change log keyed to the original language, and two remaining negotiation choices.

Title: Federal tax research plan for a property sale
Summary: Create an authority-driven research map, not a tax conclusion.
RolePerspective: Federal tax attorney preparing an issue list for tax-adviser review
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [seller type], [property use], [acquisition and improvement records], [sale terms], [tax year].
TASK: Identify federal income tax issues that counsel or a tax adviser should research, including amount realized, basis, depreciation, character, and reporting where relevant. Check current Internal Revenue Code, regulations, and IRS guidance if sources are available.
OUTPUT: Issue / missing fact / primary authority to verify / possible treatment stated conditionally / adviser question table. Do not compute liability without complete figures.

Title: Section 1031 exchange intake
Summary: Surface qualification questions and critical timing facts.
RolePerspective: Federal tax counsel coordinating a possible Section 1031 exchange
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [relinquished and replacement property facts], [owners], [closing timeline], [intermediary information], [proceeds flow].
TASK: Build a federal Section 1031 exchange intake roadmap. Verify current statutory and regulatory requirements, including eligibility, identification, timing, related parties, and intermediary issues before stating a rule.
OUTPUT: Eligibility decision tree, dated milestone worksheet with assumptions, document requests, and questions for the exchange intermediary and tax adviser. Avoid promising deferral.

Title: Federal wage and hour audit questions
Summary: Organize FLSA classification and pay evidence.
RolePerspective: Federal employment counsel reviewing wage and hour practices
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [job descriptions], [pay practices], [time records], [work location], [review period].
TASK: Identify federal FLSA wage and hour questions on coverage, exempt classification, hours worked, overtime, recordkeeping, and possible limitations. Verify current federal rules and note any Florida overlay separately.
OUTPUT: Employee group / known practice / required evidence / federal authority to check / risk question table. Do not decide exemption status without duties and pay facts.

Title: Accommodation request response map
Summary: Structure an ADA interactive-process review.
RolePerspective: Federal employment counsel preparing an accommodation process review
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [employee request], [job duties], [communications], [dates], [available alternatives].
TASK: Build a neutral chronology and issue map for a federal employment accommodation request. Identify information needed to evaluate essential functions, possible accommodations, and undue hardship under current applicable federal law, without assuming a medical conclusion.
OUTPUT: Dated events, information request list, options to discuss, decision factors with sources to verify, and a draft acknowledgement for counsel review.

Title: Condominium declaration amendment drafter
Summary: Turn approved changes into a traceable amendment and recording checklist.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium counsel drafting for [association or developer]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [current recorded declaration and amendments], [approved amendment instructions], [unit schedule and exhibits], [approval record], [effective date].
TASK: Draft only the requested amendment using existing article numbering and defined terms; show changed provisions beside current text, and identify effects on property rights, votes, mortgagee consents, exhibits, and recordability without assuming any approval occurred.
OUTPUT: A clean amendment, clause-level change table, and execution/approval/recording checklist.
CHECK: Verify current Chapter 718, governing documents, required approvals and county recording formality from primary sources before execution.

Title: Common element change instrument issue map
Summary: Plan documents and approvals for a proposed condominium property change.
RolePerspective: Florida condominium counsel coordinating a common element project
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [declaration and survey exhibits], [project plan], [affected units], [proposed allocation and cost], [board/member record].
TASK: Compare existing property descriptions with the proposed change; distinguish an operational board decision from a property-right change that may require an amendment, consent, revised exhibit, or joinder. Do not infer a unit boundary from a summary or image alone.
OUTPUT: A source-cited map of affected rights, missing consents, instrument choices, and draft language options for attorney review.
CHECK: Verify statutory and document-specific authority and confirm descriptions with appropriate survey/title professionals.

Title: HOA declaration amendment drafter
Summary: Draft a targeted covenant amendment from approved policy instructions.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel for [association or developer]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [recorded declaration and amendments], [specific policy change], [membership or developer approval record], [property description].
TASK: Draft an amendment consistent with existing definitions, exceptions, enforcement procedures, and amendment mechanics; show whether grandfathering or lender consent may matter. Separate policy proposals from actions already authorized.
OUTPUT: Clean amendment text, comparison table, unresolved approval list, and execution/recording checklist.
CHECK: Verify current Chapter 720, Chapter 712 if preservation is implicated, and the operative declaration; never assert that a vote occurred without evidence.

Title: Architectural standards rewrite
Summary: Turn design goals into administrable architectural criteria.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel revising architectural-review standards
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [declaration and design guidelines], [proposed standards], [documented complaints], [approval authority], [adoption process].
TASK: Identify ambiguous criteria, inconsistent exceptions, discretionary standards without guardrails, approval deadlines, appeal procedures, and conflicts with higher-order governing documents. Propose precise language without expanding committee power by implication.
OUTPUT: Priority issue table, clean revised standards, and adoption questions for the board.
CHECK: Check current governing documents and applicable Florida requirements before recommending a process or deadline.

Title: HOA shared amenity cost allocation
Summary: Draft a maintenance and expense allocation for shared facilities.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel negotiating shared facilities terms
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [recorded covenants], [facility plan], [users and beneficiaries], [cost data], [existing service agreements].
TASK: Define routine and capital work, access, budgeting, insurance, damage, default cure, and allocation formula; test whether a draft conflicts with recorded rights or imposes duties on nonparties.
OUTPUT: Term sheet and illustrative clause set with a table of who performs, pays, approves, and insures each task.
CHECK: Flag any property rights that require a recorded instrument, joinders, or title review.

Title: Developer turnover document plan
Summary: Build a transition packet and gap list for an HOA turnover.
RolePerspective: Florida HOA counsel preparing the transition team
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [governing documents], [turnover notices], [contracts], [financial records], [project dates], [asset list].
TASK: Map the documented turnover sequence, inventory materials received versus requested, and identify unresolved contracts, warranties, litigation, title interests, and reserves; avoid inventing a statutory deadline.
OUTPUT: Dated turnover checklist, missing-item request, responsible party, and counsel review points.
CHECK: Verify operative Chapter 720 provisions and effective dates against primary authority and the community documents.

Title: LOI-to-purchase-agreement trace
Summary: Check that the definitive purchase agreement implements an agreed LOI.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate transaction counsel for [buyer or seller]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [signed LOI], [draft purchase agreement], [deal emails expressly approved], [client position].
TASK: Extract each material LOI term, find its location in the draft, mark missing, changed, or inconsistent language, and identify matters deliberately left for negotiation. Distinguish binding LOI provisions from nonbinding discussion.
OUTPUT: Term-by-term matrix with citations, business effect, and proposed markup or question.
CHECK: Preserve the exact source wording and do not convert a negotiation point into an agreed term.

Title: Buyer diligence decision register
Summary: Prioritize property diligence findings against agreement remedies.
RolePerspective: Florida buyer-side real-estate counsel preparing a decision memo
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [purchase agreement], [inspection reports], [leases], [title and survey], [client risk priorities], [diligence end date].
TASK: Map each documented issue to the relevant contractual notice, cure, termination, escrow, price, or post-closing option; identify incomplete reports and unknowns.
OUTPUT: Decision register showing finding, source/page, severity rationale, contractual lever, owner, and next action.
CHECK: Verify contractual notice methods and dates from the executed agreement; do not calculate a deadline from missing dates.

Title: Representations and disclosure schedules
Summary: Draft aligned property sale disclosures without factual assumptions.
RolePerspective: Florida seller-side real-estate counsel preparing disclosure schedules
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [purchase agreement representations], [seller-provided facts and documents], [diligence requests], [client-approved disclosures].
TASK: Map each representation to supported exceptions; draft precise schedule entries keyed to the clause and record. Identify qualifications, cross-disclosure mechanics, and matters needing owner confirmation; do not manufacture exceptions.
OUTPUT: Representation-to-evidence table, draft schedule entries, and factual questions for the seller.
CHECK: Treat materiality and knowledge qualifiers exactly as drafted; flag changed deal positions separately.

Title: Closing condition and termination tracker
Summary: Track objective conditions, deliverables, and cure opportunities.
RolePerspective: Florida transaction counsel coordinating closing
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [executed agreement and amendments], [title and lender conditions], [approvals], [milestone dates], [correspondence].
TASK: List every condition to each party’s obligation, satisfaction evidence, waiver authority, notice and cure mechanics, and open issue. Separate a covenant from a true closing condition.
OUTPUT: Date-ordered tracker with owner, source section, status, required proof, and escalation item.
CHECK: Verify calendar calculations and notice provisions against the controlling contract before reliance.

Title: Seller exception package
Summary: Prepare a supported exceptions response to buyer diligence.
RolePerspective: Florida seller-side deal counsel writing for the buyer’s counsel
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [buyer question list], [seller-approved facts], [relevant contract language], [supporting files], [business constraints].
TASK: Draft a precise response that states only supported facts, identifies records being delivered, reserves legal positions where appropriate, and lists questions still awaiting client confirmation.
OUTPUT: Buyer-facing response plus a separate internal question and verification checklist for counsel.
CHECK: Do not imply an attachment was delivered or a condition was satisfied unless the record establishes it.

Title: Post-closing escrow and covenant plan
Summary: Allocate continuing responsibilities after a property closing.
RolePerspective: Florida closing counsel negotiating post-closing performance
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [executed agreement], [open punch list], [proposed holdback], [inspection rights], [release triggers], [client priorities].
TASK: Compare practical ways to handle specified unresolved items, including escrow, access license, holdback, price adjustment, and separate covenant; define measurable completion and dispute steps.
OUTPUT: Option table and draft term sheet with amount, custodian, milestone, notice, release, and survival questions.
CHECK: Do not state that escrow funds exist or a third party accepted duties without evidence.

Title: Title objection and cure letter
Summary: Convert title and survey issues into contract-compliant objections.
RolePerspective: Florida buyer-side title counsel writing to seller’s counsel
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [title commitment and exception instruments], [survey], [purchase agreement], [objection date].
TASK: Separate mandatory requirements from discretionary exceptions; draft numbered objections with exact instrument references and requested cure, without asserting an exception is removable merely because it is undesirable.
OUTPUT: Seller-facing objection letter and internal matrix of source, defect, proposed cure, and unresolved evidence.
CHECK: Confirm notice date and contractual objection standard before sending.

Title: Survey access and boundary gap check
Summary: Ask the right questions about a boundary or access discrepancy.
RolePerspective: Florida title counsel coordinating a licensed surveyor and title agent
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [survey], [title commitment], [recorded easements], [deeds and plats], [site facts].
TASK: Compare the mapped parcel, access routes, easement locations, improvements, encroachments, and description calls; label ambiguities requiring surveyor or title-company confirmation.
OUTPUT: Issue table with source reference, practical exposure, surveyor question, title question, and proposed cure path.
CHECK: Do not infer property boundaries or marketable access solely from a drawing.

Title: Recorded easement priority analysis
Summary: Trace easement creation, scope, successors, and possible subordination.
RolePerspective: Florida title counsel analyzing a recorded easement
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [grant and amendments], [chain of title], [mortgages], [survey], [recording dates], [use facts].
TASK: Extract the actual benefited and burdened land, permitted uses, width/location, duration, relocation, maintenance, and priority facts; identify unresolved chain or consent issues.
OUTPUT: Instrument chronology, source-cited rights matrix, and focused title/survey questions.
CHECK: Check current Florida recording and property law in primary sources; do not declare priority without a complete relevant chain.

Title: Lender title endorsement request matrix
Summary: Align lender risks to documents and insurer decisions.
RolePerspective: Florida lender-side title counsel reviewing coverage requests
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [loan terms], [title commitment], [survey], [recorded documents], [proposed endorsements].
TASK: For each lender requirement, identify the coverage question, evidence needed, insurer underwriting response, exception changes, and whether a gap requires counsel action.
OUTPUT: Coverage/requirement matrix and a short prioritized request to the title agent.
CHECK: Do not state that an endorsement is available or issued until the insurer confirms.

Title: Recorded covenant preservation research
Summary: Identify facts needed before advising on a covenant’s survival.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate counsel evaluating recorded covenant status
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [relevant root deeds], [recorded covenant and notices], [legal descriptions], [recording dates], [property type].
TASK: Construct a document chronology and a primary-source research plan for any potentially applicable marketable record title or preservation regime; identify exceptions and unanswered chain questions.
OUTPUT: Source chronology, issue list, and next-records request without a premature survival conclusion.
CHECK: Verify current Chapters 712 and 720 where relevant and check actual record evidence; do not assume a covenant has expired.

Title: Retail use and exclusivity redline
Summary: Clarify permitted use, exclusivity, and landlord remedies.
RolePerspective: Florida retail leasing counsel for [landlord or tenant]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [lease draft], [tenant business model], [tenant mix], [existing exclusives], [deal term sheet].
TASK: Compare permitted use, prohibited activities, exclusivity radius and exceptions, cure, remedies, and successor applicability; propose balanced language that does not promise control over unrelated properties.
OUTPUT: Clause-by-clause redline instructions, revised provisions, and open commercial questions.
CHECK: Match defined terms and any existing center-wide restrictions to documents actually supplied.

Title: Operating expense pass-through audit
Summary: Review a commercial lease CAM reconciliation.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial leasing counsel for [tenant or landlord]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [executed lease], [CAM statement], [budget and invoices], [prior reconciliations], [gross-up method].
TASK: Map billed categories and allocation formulas to lease clauses; separate math questions from contract interpretation and identify exclusions, caps, base year, audit rights, and required supporting records.
OUTPUT: Charge-to-clause table, recalculation questions, potential credits, and a measured records request.
CHECK: Do not assert that a charge violates the lease without tracing both the contract text and underlying data.

Title: Tenant improvement work letter
Summary: Draft milestone and change-order mechanics for a buildout.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial leasing counsel negotiating a work letter
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [lease economics], [plans/specifications], [landlord and tenant responsibilities], [allowance], [delivery schedule].
TASK: Allocate design approval, permits, contractor selection, schedule extensions, change orders, allowance draws, lien protection, substantial completion, and punch list. Distinguish a target date from a guaranteed date.
OUTPUT: Work letter clauses and a responsibility/milestone table.
CHECK: Flag code, license, permit, and lien issues requiring specialist or current-law review.

Title: SNDA and estoppel consistency check
Summary: Compare a lease to lender and estoppel forms.
RolePerspective: Florida leasing counsel for [tenant, landlord, or lender]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [executed lease and amendments], [proposed SNDA], [estoppel form], [loan context], [known defaults].
TASK: Mark statements that exceed documented knowledge, modify rent or options, waive defenses, affect nondisturbance, or impose notice and cure obligations; distinguish a factual certificate from a contract amendment.
OUTPUT: Variance matrix and clean issue list with proposed narrow corrections.
CHECK: Never certify occupancy, absence of default, or payment amounts without client confirmation.

Title: Residential lease notice and deposit workflow
Summary: Build a Florida residential termination or deposit response plan.
RolePerspective: Florida residential leasing counsel for [landlord or tenant]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [executed lease], [payment ledger], [move-in/out records], [notices and delivery evidence], [key dates].
TASK: Organize factual timeline, classify the requested action, identify lease terms and statutory issues to research, and draft only the next appropriate communication after facts are confirmed.
OUTPUT: Event timeline, missing-evidence list, applicable-notice research checklist, and draft communication.
CHECK: Verify current Chapter 83 Part II and any applicable local/federal overlay; do not invent a deadline or assume valid service.

Title: Zoning verification evidence packet
Summary: Prepare the inputs for a site-specific zoning inquiry.
RolePerspective: Florida land-use counsel preparing a zoning verification request
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [parcel identifiers], [current zoning map], [applicable ordinances], [existing uses], [proposed use], [historic approvals].
TASK: Separate legal lot, current use, proposed use, district rules, variances, overlays, and prior approvals; identify the precise questions for staff rather than inferring entitlement from a map legend.
OUTPUT: Verification request with labeled exhibits and an unresolved fact/source list.
CHECK: Check current local code, plan, maps, and written interpretations as of the relevant date.

Title: Conditional use hearing record builder
Summary: Structure testimony and exhibits around approval criteria.
RolePerspective: Florida land-use counsel preparing an applicant for a local hearing
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [application], [staff report], [ordinance criteria], [traffic/environmental reports], [public comments], [hearing date].
TASK: Match each criterion to record evidence, gaps, likely objections, and a witness with firsthand foundation. Distinguish staff conclusions from evidence and avoid unsupported promises about impacts.
OUTPUT: Criterion-by-criterion hearing matrix, exhibit list, and concise witness question outlines.
CHECK: Verify current local procedure, disclosure rules, and hearing record requirements.

Title: Development approval conditions tracker
Summary: Turn approvals into assigned deliverables and timing controls.
RolePerspective: Florida development counsel coordinating permits and consultants
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [development order], [site plan approvals], [permits], [agency comments], [project schedule].
TASK: Extract each condition’s text, who must perform it, triggering event, evidence of completion, dependencies, and potential amendment path. Distinguish preconstruction, pre-CO, and ongoing obligations only when the document supports that grouping.
OUTPUT: Condition matrix with verbatim source references, owners, open evidence, and escalation notes.
CHECK: Check effective dates and actual approval documents; do not assume a condition has been satisfied.

Title: Development agreement negotiation map
Summary: Align public obligations with private project milestones.
RolePerspective: Florida developer-side land-use counsel preparing a term negotiation
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [draft agreement], [site plan], [infrastructure budget], [agency comments], [project phases].
TASK: Compare alternatives for improvements, phasing, bonding, vesting, public access, reimbursements, defaults, and assignment; flag obligations needing separate approvals or recorded instruments.
OUTPUT: Negotiation matrix with proposed language concepts, business tradeoffs, and unresolved approvals.
CHECK: Verify current local and Florida statutory authority for the contemplated agreement and its approval process.

Title: Permit denial response map
Summary: Identify record and timing questions after an adverse local decision.
RolePerspective: Florida land-use counsel assessing a permitting setback
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [application], [written decision], [notice/service proof], [local code], [hearing record], [decision date].
TASK: Separate reasons actually stated from inferred grounds; identify potentially available reconsideration, administrative, judicial, or resubmission avenues without selecting one before confirming jurisdiction and deadlines.
OUTPUT: Dated option chart, missing record list, and questions for immediate deadline verification.
CHECK: Check current local and state procedural authority and actual delivery dates before stating a filing deadline.

Title: Litigation hold and ESI source map
Summary: Plan preservation by custodians, systems, and evidence risk.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigation counsel directing preservation
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [claim and defense outline], [known custodians], [systems], [retention policies], [incident dates].
TASK: Identify likely documents and ESI, ephemeral sources, preservation owners, potentially conflicting retention practices, and information needed to scope a proportionate hold; do not assume a system contains responsive data.
OUTPUT: Custodian/system matrix, draft hold notice for counsel review, and collection questions.
CHECK: Verify current duty triggers, protective orders, and applicable Florida discovery rules as of the case date.

Title: Initial disclosure source inventory
Summary: Prepare a Florida civil case disclosure plan from the actual file.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigator organizing discovery obligations
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [operative pleadings], [case management order], [custodian list], [known documents], [insurance records].
TASK: Map claims and defenses to likely witnesses, documents, damages information, and insurance material; flag sources not yet reviewed and what the applicable order requires.
OUTPUT: Disclosure-ready fact inventory with provenance, owner, gaps, and a rule/order verification checklist.
CHECK: Check current Florida Rules of Civil Procedure and the case-specific order; do not treat a draft inventory as a filed disclosure.

Title: Targeted production requests
Summary: Draft proportionate document requests tied to pleaded issues.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigation counsel drafting requests for production
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [operative pleadings], [claims/defenses matrix], [known record gaps], [custodians], [case order].
TASK: Draft numbered requests keyed to disputed elements and reasonably described records; consider date ranges, ESI format, burden, privilege, and protective order issues. Remove duplicative or fishing-expedition requests.
OUTPUT: Request set with purpose, element, likely custodian, and proposed scope note for each item.
CHECK: Check current Florida rules, discovery limits, and court order before service.

Title: Privilege log sufficiency review
Summary: Identify missing information and possible privilege questions.
RolePerspective: Florida litigation counsel reviewing a production and privilege log
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [log], [requests and responses], [production index], [protective order], [known communication context].
TASK: Compare each withheld item to the asserted basis and available sender/recipient/date/subject information; flag gaps, inconsistent treatment, and nonprivileged attachments without deciding privilege from a label alone.
OUTPUT: Item-level question matrix and a prioritized meet-and-confer agenda.
CHECK: Apply current Florida privilege and procedure rules and preserve confidentiality during review.

Title: Discovery deficiency conference letter
Summary: Draft a specific, supportable meet-and-confer request.
RolePerspective: Florida litigation counsel writing to opposing counsel
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [requests], [responses/objections], [production], [prior correspondence], [case order].
TASK: For each deficiency, quote or cite the request and response accurately, explain what remains missing and why material, and propose a reasonable cure or compromise. Avoid accusing counsel of concealment without evidence.
OUTPUT: Professional letter and internal issue table with source location and proposed resolution.
CHECK: Check governing Florida rule, local requirements, order, and response dates before threatening motion practice.

Title: Summary judgment record matrix
Summary: Connect every proposed fact to admissible record material.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigator preparing a summary judgment record
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [operative pleadings], [depositions], [declarations], [exhibits], [proposed motion], [case schedule].
TASK: List material elements, proposed undisputed facts, exact supporting and contrary citations, evidentiary objections, and missing authentication; distinguish lawyer argument from record fact.
OUTPUT: Two-sided fact matrix, proposed issue outline, and factual statements requiring manual verification.
CHECK: Verify current Florida summary judgment rule, controlling decisions, citation accuracy, and case order before filing.

Title: Injunction evidence and remedy map
Summary: Test requested interim relief against proof and feasibility.
RolePerspective: Florida civil litigator evaluating interim relief
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [verified complaint or proposed pleading], [declarations], [contract], [harm record], [opposing evidence], [hearing date].
TASK: Identify each element to establish under current Florida law, proof available or missing, remedy breadth, practical enforcement, and defenses; distinguish irreparable harm evidence from conclusory language.
OUTPUT: Element/evidence matrix, narrowly tailored proposed remedy outline, and urgent verification questions.
CHECK: Check current Florida procedure, notice, bond, and controlling law before any filing or client assurance.

Title: Expert opinion foundation audit
Summary: Stress-test an expert report and its source chain.
RolePerspective: Florida litigation counsel preparing for expert discovery
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [expert report], [data and assumptions], [CV], [underlying publications], [case schedule].
TASK: Identify each opinion, factual inputs, method, limiting assumptions, internal inconsistencies, and points the report does not support. Develop questions on reliability and fit without inventing studies or expert admissions.
OUTPUT: Opinion-to-source chart, prioritized deposition topics, and missing disclosure requests.
CHECK: Verify applicable Florida evidentiary standard, current disclosure rules, and court orders before litigation use.

Title: Trial exhibit foundation checklist
Summary: Prepare witness and objection questions for each exhibit.
RolePerspective: Florida trial counsel organizing exhibit admission
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [proposed exhibits], [witness list], [depositions], [stipulations], [pretrial order].
TASK: For each exhibit identify the proposition it supports, sponsoring witness, authenticating facts, hearsay concerns and potential exceptions, redactions, and any disputed foundation.
OUTPUT: Exhibit table, witness-specific foundation questions, and unresolved stipulation requests.
CHECK: Verify current Florida Evidence Code, order, and actual exhibit versions; do not invent testimony.

Title: Post-trial preservation and deadline map
Summary: Inventory issues to preserve and time-sensitive next steps.
RolePerspective: Florida appellate-aware trial counsel preparing after a judgment
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [judgment/order], [service/filing timestamps], [trial record], [motions and objections], [case docket].
TASK: Map potential post-trial and appellate steps to the ruling, preservation status, missing transcript or record, and critical dates; state competing interpretations where the record or service date is uncertain.
OUTPUT: Dated action chart, preservation question list, and assignments for immediate verification.
CHECK: Confirm current appellate and civil rules, court orders, and exact triggering events; do not compute deadlines from assumed dates.

Title: Executive options memo
Summary: Condense a complex legal issue into a decision for a business client.
RolePerspective: Florida outside counsel advising a business decision-maker
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [confirmed facts], [source documents], [verified legal analysis], [client objective], [decision deadline].
TASK: State the decision required, supported facts, legal constraints, two or three viable options with cost/risk/tradeoffs, and what new fact would change the recommendation. Separate legal conclusion from commercial judgment.
OUTPUT: One-page executive memo and an appendix listing authorities or document sections actually checked.
CHECK: Do not present an unverified rule or fact as resolved; flag the review steps before client delivery.

Title: Board decision brief for a disputed contract
Summary: Present a neutral action choice to a nonlawyer board.
RolePerspective: Florida board counsel advising directors
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [contract], [performance history], [counsel-verified rights], [financial options], [conflicts information].
TASK: Explain the question in plain English; compare performance, negotiated resolution, notice/cure, and litigation if realistically available. Identify possible conflicts and who has authority to act; avoid assuming a board vote.
OUTPUT: Two-page board brief, options table, and proposed questions for an executive session.
CHECK: Confirm privilege handling, actual governance documents, and applicable Florida requirements.

Title: Adverse development client update
Summary: Communicate bad news with accurate next steps and no false reassurance.
RolePerspective: Florida lead counsel updating a client after an adverse event
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [order or event report], [verified facts], [open deadlines], [client priorities], [proposed response].
TASK: State what happened, what is confirmed versus uncertain, immediate consequence, available next decisions, and information counsel is checking. Use measured language and avoid guaranteeing an outcome.
OUTPUT: Client-ready email under 350 words plus an internal verification and follow-up list.
CHECK: Verify order text and operative dates before communicating any legal deadline.

Title: Negotiation instruction email
Summary: Obtain specific client authority on deal tradeoffs.
RolePerspective: Florida transaction counsel seeking client instructions
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [counterparty markup], [term sheet], [client redlines], [financial consequences], [decision deadline].
TASK: Group decisions into must-have, negotiable, and defer; explain the business implication of each open point and identify concessions requiring explicit approval. Do not imply authority to concede an item.
OUTPUT: Short email with a numbered decision checklist and recommended fallback positions clearly marked for approval.
CHECK: Confirm any stated monetary impact against approved deal data.

Title: Florida entity choice issue map
Summary: Compare corporation and LLC structures for a particular venture.
RolePerspective: Florida business organizations counsel advising founders
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [founder goals], [ownership and capital plan], [management needs], [investor expectations], [tax-adviser input].
TASK: Compare governance, transfer, liability, formation, financing, and exit implications under current Florida law; identify separate federal and state tax questions for tax counsel instead of selecting tax treatment without facts.
OUTPUT: Decision table, threshold questions, and conditional recommendation for counsel discussion.
CHECK: Check current Chapters 605 and 607 and do not claim a tax advantage without competent tax analysis.

Title: Two-member LLC operating agreement
Summary: Outline governance and deadlock mechanisms for a Florida LLC.
RolePerspective: Florida LLC counsel drafting for [company or named member]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [ownership and contributions], [management structure], [distribution priorities], [exit goals], [approved business terms].
TASK: Draft governance architecture addressing reserved matters, signatures, budgets, additional capital, transfer, deadlock escalation, buyout triggers, records, dissolution, and dispute resolution. Mark choices that require client instructions.
OUTPUT: Annotated term sheet and clause set with a decision list for both owners.
CHECK: Verify current Chapter 605 defaults and nonwaivable limits before drafting operative provisions.

Title: Member admission and cap table reconciliation
Summary: Trace a new investor’s rights into LLC documents.
RolePerspective: Florida company counsel preparing an LLC admission
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [operating agreement], [cap table], [subscription terms], [contribution records], [approvals].
TASK: Compare proposed units or percentages, dilution, voting, distributions, transfer limits, and required consents to the existing documents; do not infer a completed admission from a draft spreadsheet.
OUTPUT: Before/after ownership table, required-document list, and issues for tax and securities counsel.
CHECK: Verify the governing agreement and current Florida law; label numerical assumptions and reconcile totals.

Title: Board or member written consent package
Summary: Draft action records that match the entity’s actual authority.
RolePerspective: Florida corporate counsel preparing formal approvals
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [organizational documents], [proposed transaction], [conflict disclosures], [signatory roster], [required approvals].
TASK: Identify which body may act and by which procedure; draft recitals and resolutions limited to actions evidenced or proposed. Distinguish an approval to negotiate from final authorization to execute.
OUTPUT: Draft consent or minutes, officer certificate outline, and signing/notice checklist.
CHECK: Verify Chapters 605 or 607, bylaws/operating agreement, quorum, conflicts, and any third-party consent.

Title: Interested-director transaction review
Summary: Create a factual record and approval question map.
RolePerspective: Florida corporation counsel advising disinterested decision-makers
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [proposed transaction], [conflict disclosures], [board materials], [comparables], [governing documents].
TASK: Identify the nature of each interest, what was disclosed, alternatives considered, participation or recusal facts, and potentially relevant approval standards; do not declare fairness from the client’s stated price alone.
OUTPUT: Fact-and-authority table, missing-information request, and draft neutral board discussion agenda.
CHECK: Verify current Florida corporate provisions and governing documents before recommending a safe harbor.

Title: Shareholder transfer restriction clauses
Summary: Draft a coherent right of first refusal and buy-sell sequence.
RolePerspective: Florida closely held company counsel drafting for [company or shareholder]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [articles and bylaws], [ownership table], [term sheet], [valuation process], [financing constraints].
TASK: Draft notice, permitted transfers, offer matching, valuation, payment, deadlock, death/disability, and enforcement mechanics; test timelines against one another and conflicts with existing instruments.
OUTPUT: Integrated clause set and example transfer timeline with alternatives requiring business approval.
CHECK: Verify current Chapter 607 and any securities or tax questions with relevant specialists.

Title: Asset sale approval and consent map
Summary: Check who must approve a Florida company’s asset sale.
RolePerspective: Florida transaction counsel coordinating entity approvals
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [entity type and documents], [draft asset purchase agreement], [asset schedule], [debt contracts], [ownership information].
TASK: Identify possible internal approvals, lienholder/contract consents, assignment restrictions, solvency or distribution questions, and uncertain statutory thresholds; separate an asset sale from a merger.
OUTPUT: Approval matrix with source, decision-maker, signature authority, evidence needed, and critical sequencing.
CHECK: Check current Chapter 605 or 607, governing documents, and actual contracts before stating a vote threshold.

Title: Florida entity dissolution plan
Summary: Inventory obligations before voluntary dissolution and winding up.
RolePerspective: Florida company counsel planning an orderly wind-up
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [entity records], [liabilities], [pending contracts and claims], [tax-adviser input], [distribution proposal].
TASK: Map approvals, claims handling, creditor notices, contract termination, asset disposition, reserves, tax coordination, and final filings; distinguish a proposed step from an accomplished one.
OUTPUT: Phase-by-phase checklist with owners, supporting records, open liabilities, and distribution hold points.
CHECK: Verify current entity statute and applicable claims procedures rather than assuming a fixed notice period.

Title: Master services agreement risk redline
Summary: Prioritize negotiable contract risk from one party’s viewpoint.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial contracts counsel for [customer or provider]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [MSA draft], [statement of work], [business model], [insurance], [negotiation guardrails].
TASK: Identify scope drift, acceptance, payment, personnel, confidentiality, IP, warranties, indemnities, liability cap, termination, and order of precedence; propose proportional fixes.
OUTPUT: Issue matrix with clause, practical scenario, priority, fallback, and concise proposed text.
CHECK: Quote operative contract language accurately and flag governing-law issues for verification.

Title: SaaS and data processing terms
Summary: Align SaaS promises with actual services and data handling.
RolePerspective: Florida technology contracts counsel for [customer or provider]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [SaaS order], [MSA/DPA], [security materials], [data-flow description], [service levels].
TASK: Map data categories, access, incident notice, subprocessors, retention/deletion, audit rights, service credits, and intellectual property ownership to documented capabilities; identify mismatches without inventing compliance certifications.
OUTPUT: Clause-to-operational-evidence matrix, proposed changes, and questions for security/privacy personnel.
CHECK: Confirm which privacy and breach-notice laws actually apply and verify current requirements with primary sources.

Title: Intellectual property ownership clause
Summary: Distinguish background IP, deliverables, licenses, and third-party material.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial counsel negotiating a work product agreement
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [scope of work], [existing IP inventory], [third-party components], [commercial term sheet], [draft contract].
TASK: Define created deliverables, retained tools and know-how, license scope, sublicensing, embedded third-party terms, payment conditions, and transition rights; test whether ownership and license promises can both be performed.
OUTPUT: Alternative clause set for each party and a rights table by asset type.
CHECK: Flag applicable federal copyright, trade secret, and open-source questions for specialist review.

Title: Indemnity and liability cap stress test
Summary: Model how risk clauses interact under concrete claims.
RolePerspective: Florida contract counsel negotiating indemnity and liability limits
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [draft agreement], [insurance schedule], [service risks], [client exposure preferences].
TASK: Test third-party versus first-party claims, defense control, procedures, exclusions, damages waivers, supercaps, carveouts, survival, and whether insurance actually supports the proposed allocation.
OUTPUT: Three claim scenarios, clause interaction matrix, and narrow revised text with fallback positions.
CHECK: Do not claim insurance coverage or enforceability absent policy text and current governing law.

Title: Mutual confidentiality agreement repair
Summary: Draft usable confidential-information rules with practical exceptions.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial contracts counsel for [disclosing or receiving party]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [NDA], [purpose of discussions], [expected recipients], [retention practices], [regulatory constraints].
TASK: Check definition, exclusions, representative access, compelled disclosure, return/destruction, residual knowledge, publicity, term, injunctive relief, and how the NDA interacts with later agreements.
OUTPUT: Clean clause revisions and a short list of business choices needed before circulation.
CHECK: Avoid stating that confidentiality alone ensures privilege or data-law compliance.

Title: Termination and transition clause
Summary: Design a workable exit from a long-running service arrangement.
RolePerspective: Florida commercial contract counsel representing [customer or provider]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [contract draft], [dependencies], [critical data], [transition period], [payment status].
TASK: Compare termination for cause/convenience, cure, disputed invoices, continued service, data export, transition assistance, fees, and survival; test how each path operates after an incident.
OUTPUT: Exit-scenario table and integrated termination/transition clause options.
CHECK: Check conflict with existing service-level, confidentiality, and license terms.

Title: Statement of work and change-control template
Summary: Build measurable deliverables and approval steps.
RolePerspective: Florida contract counsel drafting a project SOW
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [scope notes], [project schedule], [price model], [dependencies], [acceptance criteria].
TASK: Translate scope into deliverables, objective acceptance tests, responsibilities, assumptions, dependencies, change-request approval, schedule effects, and payment milestones. Do not fill missing budgets or acceptance standards with invented facts.
OUTPUT: SOW skeleton, sample change-order form, and decision list for project managers.
CHECK: Reconcile all definitions and order-of-precedence language with the master agreement.

Title: Permanent access easement grant
Summary: Draft rights that are specific enough to record and administer.
RolePerspective: Florida real-property counsel for [grantor or grantee]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [servient and dominant title], [surveyor exhibit], [use plan], [maintenance proposal], [existing liens].
TASK: Draft grant, benefited/burdened land, location exhibit reference, permitted users and vehicles, relocation, maintenance, insurance, duration, default, successors, and mortgagee questions; do not draw a legal description.
OUTPUT: Recordable-form draft with blanks for surveyor/title confirmation and a rights/responsibilities table.
CHECK: Verify the actual legal descriptions, authority, joinders, and recording formalities before execution.

Title: Reciprocal easement agreement architecture
Summary: Coordinate shared access, utilities, and parking across parcels.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate counsel drafting a reciprocal easement agreement
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [parcel deeds and plats], [site plan], [parking allocation], [utility routes], [lender positions].
TASK: Map each parcel’s grants and reservations, user classes, relocation rights, maintenance, costs, insurance, casualty, enforcement, subdivision, and successor obligations. Test whether reciprocal rights conflict with an existing restriction.
OUTPUT: Grant matrix by parcel, clause outline, exhibit list, and unresolved survey/lender questions.
CHECK: Require precise survey exhibits and verify existing priority and consent before final language.

Title: Restrictive covenant declaration drafting
Summary: Draft use restrictions with clear burden, benefit, and enforcement.
RolePerspective: Florida property counsel for [developer or benefiting owner]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [tract descriptions], [business objective], [plat], [existing recorded restrictions], [approval record].
TASK: State affected land and beneficiaries, restrictions and exceptions, enforcement rights, amendment/termination method, duration, and dispute process. Compare the proposed restriction to zoning and other recorded limits without assuming it overrides them.
OUTPUT: Recordable-form declaration, definitions list, and a schedule of open consents/exhibits.
CHECK: Verify current Florida property and recording law, marketable title issues, and authority of every signer.

Title: Temporary construction easement
Summary: Limit temporary work rights by area, time, restoration, and risk.
RolePerspective: Florida owner-side property counsel negotiating construction access
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [work plans], [survey sketch], [construction schedule], [insurance], [property conditions].
TASK: Define exact permitted work, staging, hours, ingress, notice, damage repair, safety, indemnity, insurance, liens, restoration standard, inspection, and termination; distinguish license from easement if material.
OUTPUT: Term sheet and draft provisions with unresolved technical exhibits marked.
CHECK: Confirm the legal description and project permits with the relevant professionals; do not imply permits exist.

Title: Shared facility maintenance agreement
Summary: Allocate upkeep of a private road or drainage facility.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate counsel for [one or more neighboring owners]
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [recorded easement], [facility plans], [current users], [anticipated costs], [insurance].
TASK: Define scope of routine, emergency, and capital work; budgeting and assessments; access for repair; contractor decisions; insurance; default remedies; and dispute resolution. Reconcile duties with the underlying easement and government obligations.
OUTPUT: Recorded-agreement outline, allocation table, and a list of survey/engineering questions.
CHECK: Verify party authority, permitted recordation, and whether nonparties need to join.

Title: Recordable instrument execution audit
Summary: Check a deed, easement, or declaration package before signing.
RolePerspective: Florida real-estate counsel checking a recording package
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [near-final instrument], [title commitment], [survey/description exhibit], [entity authority], [county recording instructions].
TASK: Check parties, legal names, property description, defined terms, exhibits, signature/acknowledgment blocks, witnesses or notarial requirements if applicable, lender/other joinders, cross-references, and documentary-stamp questions.
OUTPUT: Execution checklist with page references, open prerequisites, and a final compare-to-signed-copy step.
CHECK: Confirm current Florida and county-specific recordability requirements rather than assuming every instrument uses the same form.

Title: Partnership distribution basis issue list
Summary: Identify federal tax questions before a partnership distribution.
RolePerspective: Federal tax counsel coordinating with the partnership tax adviser
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [operating agreement], [tax basis schedules], [capital accounts], [asset values], [proposed distribution].
TASK: Separate cash, property, liabilities, partner basis, inside basis, potential gain recognition, and future allocations; identify missing K-1 and election information.
OUTPUT: Partner-by-partner fact request and primary-source research matrix with scenarios requiring calculation.
CHECK: Verify current Internal Revenue Code, regulations, and IRS guidance; do not infer tax basis from book capital.

Title: Depreciation and cost-segregation diligence
Summary: Plan tax-adviser review of a property acquisition.
RolePerspective: Federal tax counsel coordinating property-tax analysis
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [purchase allocation], [improvement invoices], [asset list], [placed-in-service evidence], [taxpayer facts].
TASK: Map assets to factual classification questions and supporting records, distinguish land from improvements and repair from capital expenditure issues, and identify potential recapture or election effects.
OUTPUT: Evidence request and asset-level issue table for a qualified tax adviser.
CHECK: Check current federal tax rules, effective dates, and any applicable state overlay; do not supply unsupported recovery periods.

Title: Installment sale structuring questions
Summary: Prepare a federal tax issue map for deferred purchase price.
RolePerspective: Federal tax attorney advising on a proposed business or property sale
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [sale agreement], [basis and debt data], [payment schedule], [asset allocation], [seller entity type].
TASK: Identify facts needed to analyze eligibility, timing of gain, interest, depreciation recapture, debt relief, contingent payments, and related-party concerns. Separate contract cash flow from recognized tax gain.
OUTPUT: Issue list with relevant facts, primary authorities to verify, and tax-adviser modeling requests.
CHECK: Check current Code, regulations, and IRS instructions; do not promise deferral without a transaction-specific computation.

Title: Section 754 election decision packet
Summary: Coordinate a partnership basis adjustment decision.
RolePerspective: Federal tax counsel preparing questions for a partnership adviser
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [partnership agreement], [interest transfer/distribution facts], [basis schedules], [return filing history].
TASK: Identify the triggering transaction, historic elections, inside/outside basis evidence, administrative cost, and partner-level effects; separate the question of whether an election exists from whether one should be made.
OUTPUT: Decision packet with fact gaps, filing questions, alternative scenarios, and adviser assignments.
CHECK: Verify current IRC sections 734, 743, 754 and applicable regulations; do not claim an election was filed without return evidence.

Title: FMLA and ADA overlap workplan
Summary: Coordinate leave and accommodation review without medical assumptions.
RolePerspective: Federal employment counsel advising an employer
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [leave request], [job description], [eligibility facts], [communications], [dates], [benefit policies].
TASK: Build a timeline of requests and employer responses, distinguish leave entitlement from accommodation questions, and identify required medical information and possible alternatives without diagnosing the employee.
OUTPUT: Timeline, information-request list, interactive-process questions, and review points for HR.
CHECK: Verify current FMLA and ADA primary authority, applicable state law, and actual coverage facts before giving a deadline or determination.

Title: FLSA exemption duties evidence audit
Summary: Gather the right facts before classifying salaried roles.
RolePerspective: Federal wage-and-hour counsel advising an employer
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [job descriptions], [actual duty interviews], [pay data], [time records], [work locations].
TASK: Compare claimed classification to actual primary duties, discretion, supervision, pay practices, and potential hours worked; identify differences by employee group and any state-law overlay.
OUTPUT: Job-family evidence matrix, missing interview questions, and possible remediation decisions for counsel.
CHECK: Check current federal regulations, effective court orders, and applicable state rules; do not decide status from title or salary alone.

Title: Workplace harassment investigation plan
Summary: Build an impartial fact investigation with protected information controls.
RolePerspective: Federal employment counsel overseeing an internal investigation
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [reported allegations], [policies], [potential witnesses], [messages], [relevant dates], [conflicts].
TASK: Separate allegations from verified facts, sequence interviews, identify document and ESI preservation, assess interim measures and retaliation risks, and avoid pre-judging credibility or outcome.
OUTPUT: Investigation plan, witness question themes, evidence map, and decision points for an independent reviewer.
CHECK: Verify current applicable federal and state law, privilege scope, and confidentiality communications with counsel.

Title: EEOC charge response record map
Summary: Organize a federal agency position statement around supportable evidence.
RolePerspective: Federal employment counsel preparing an employer response
PromptBody:
INPUTS: [charge and notice], [personnel records], [policies], [decision-maker interviews], [comparators], [submission date].
TASK: Map each allegation to company response, exact supporting documents, witnesses, relevant comparators, counterevidence, and missing facts; avoid unsupported claims about motive or employee credibility.
OUTPUT: Source-cited response outline, exhibit index, factual gaps, and review checklist for counsel.
CHECK: Confirm the actual response date, preservation obligations, agency instructions, and current applicable law before submission.
